terms.title: Interpreter’s notebook
terms.goal: Translate exactly what the delegate said.
terms.background: Helen interprets between the American and Chinese delegations. Both sides say they have a working space-fold engine. Her rule: an interpreter adds nothing and removes nothing.

lead.new: helen|My card had two words he might use. One meant a technical demonstration. The other meant a performance, as on a stage.
helen|My rule never changes. An interpreter adds nothing and removes nothing.

terms.prompt: How should Helen say it in English, and what should she note?
terms.instruction: Helen’s glossary card: yanshi means a technical demonstration. Biaoyan means a performance, as on a stage. The delegate said: bijiao women de biaoyan. Say exactly what he said, and note anything that matters.

rows.label: Say it in English
options: He proposes testing which side is stronger

rows.label: Note in shorthand
options: He agreed to a strength test

hints: Find the last word he said on Helen’s glossary card.
An interpreter adds nothing and removes nothing. Use the meaning the card gives for his word.
He did not use the demonstration word. Say what his word means, and note that he picked it on purpose.

confess.title: Joint statement

lead.new: helen|Both men were waiting for the other to blink. Somebody had to ask the first question, and it had to be me.

lead: general_us|Our observers saw a ring of light on your screen. We were never allowed inside your room.
general_cn|Our observers saw a ring of light on yours. We never went inside your room either.

lead.new: helen|Each man could only speak for his own machine. And the joint minutes would be read by the whole world.

confess.goal: Help each side say what really happened, one machine at a time.
confess.background: Each side’s observers saw a ring of light on the other side’s screen. Neither side went into the other’s room, so each man can only explain his own machine. The joint minutes will be public.
confess.prompt: Pick Helen’s question for both men, and the line for the public minutes.
confess.instruction: Ask a question each man can answer honestly about his own room. In the public minutes, write only what both sides saw.

options: What produced the ring in your room?
How did the other team produce its ring?
How far did the other team move the target?

rows.label: Write in the public minutes
options: Two projectors, one in each room
Both observers saw a ring of light
Both targets moved the same distance

hints: Each man knows his own room. Neither has seen inside the other’s.
Ask each man about something he can answer for himself.
The public minutes hold only what both sides watched happen. What did both observers see?

confess.finding: helen|Each delegate described his own machine, and neither had an engine. In the joint minutes we wrote only what both sides saw: a ring of light.

recap: helen|Both demonstrations were staged. Both sides admitted it, in this room, to each other. Then they agreed to keep lying, together.

outro.new: helen|When they understood that they had bluffed each other, the whole room laughed. Tired laughter. The kind that lets you breathe.

lines: helen|Coffee, General? It comes from the machine in the hall.
general_us|Is it any good, Mrs. Mercer?
helen|No. But it is hot, and it doesn’t pretend to be anything else.
general_us|We put our test out on open radio. Every ham in three states heard it.
helen|My husband is a ham. He talked about it at dinner for a week.
general_us|Then I hope your husband enjoyed the show.
general_cn|Your building has no windows, Mrs. Mercer. And no tea.
helen|I brought my own. Jasmine. There is enough for two.
general_cn|Then this meeting has already gone better than I expected.
general_cn|You choose your words very carefully. Who taught you?
helen|My mother. Now my son corrects me. He records everything, even the kettle.
general_cn|A family of listeners. That is rare these days.

c8_lab.objective: Work out how the fleet found Earth, and what Shaw’s old reactor can still do.
changes: plot (Mrs. Penhallow is in the lab in person)
notes: C33 turned Mrs. Penhallow’s line into a memory. The plot puts her in the lab in person (‘Nobody saw her come in’), which keeps her pattern of turning up far from her pier, so she is present here.

Art (recommended): an insert of Helen’s last notebook page: three pencil strokes, the second joined to the first and climbing higher, a gap, then one long stroke lower than both, with her margin note ‘repeats after the low note’. Reuse it in c9_choir.wick and postcredits.answer.
New sound asset for lastpage: effect.wick_high_ending (0.8 s at 220 Hz joined to 1.1 s at 330 Hz, 0.5 s silence, 2.0 s at 440 Hz). Reel 07 is effect.ninth_night; Reel 11 is effect.wick.
Saren’s ultimatum goes out on every screen and radio in the county (broadcast).
context: steve|Shaw took us into the Meridian laboratory. It was a film set. The doors were painted on the walls.
steve|The reactor was a stack of washing-machine drums, theater lights and a fog machine.

intro.text: Your mother wrote ‘heard this before’ beside a drum beat that isn’t there. I want to know where she heard it.

intro: wen|Mine fooled six. And a premier.

notebook.title: Helen’s shorthand
notebook.goal: Work out how the fleet found Earth.
notebook.background: Wen can read Helen’s shorthand, but the pages have come loose. Helen kept a scrap on each Meridian test, and notes on the meeting where both sides confessed. Beside the missing beat she wrote “heard this before”.
lead: wen|Help me put her pages back in order.
wen|This scrap is the American test. Two drum strikes, a missing beat, then a lamp flare.
wen|This one is our test. Before we built it, we were sent a copy of the American test to study.
wen|Both tests went out over open radio. Anyone with a receiver could hear them.
wen|And the minutes of the meeting at one table quote both tests. Your mother was in that room.
notebook.prompt: How did the old tests reach the fleet?

board.instruction: Use Helen’s scraps to answer four questions about the old tests.
evidence: Scrap H, the American test: two drum strikes, a missing beat, then a lamp flare.
Scrap W, the Chinese test: Wen’s team studied a copy of the American test before they built it.
Both tests went out over open radio, so anyone listening could record them.
The minutes of the meeting at one table quote both tests.

stages.prompt: Put one card on each question.
slots: How was the Chinese test built?
pieces: From a copy of the American test

board.wrong_text: Wen taps a scrap. “Your mother would not have filed it that way.”

hints: A copy can’t be made before the thing it copies.
The meeting quotes both tests, so it must come after them.
Open radio is not private. Think about who else might have been listening.
lines: c8_lab.notebook.01
steve|Heard this before. Mom heard that missing beat in the bay. In Dad’s reels.
notebook.finding: steve|America staged its test first, and China built its own from a copy, missing beat and all. Both went out over open radio, and something out there recorded them. Mom heard that same missing beat again, in the bay. The fleet came because of a show.

props.title: The reactor
props.goal: Find the two effects that must fire on the same cue.
props.background: Shaw built effects for films before she built this. Her reactor has three effects: drums, lamps and fog. Her film log records every frame of the old test.
lead: shaw|Film log’s on the clipboard. Tell me what you see.
shaw|Drums, lamps and fog. If two effects hit on the very same frames, one cue can drive them both.
shaw|Ignore anything marked rehearsal. That was me testing bulbs.
props.prompt: Shaw’s film log. Drums hit on frames 120, 128 and 136. Lamps flash on 120, 128 and 136, plus two rehearsal flashes at 112 and 144. Fog runs from frame 100 to 190. Which two effects can share one cue?

wrong.1: The fog starts at 100 and drifts to 190. It doesn’t start with anything.
wrong.2: The fog runs long before and after the drums. They don’t share a start.

hints: Look for two effects that hit on the same frames.
The fog runs the whole time. It never hits on a single frame.
Leave out the rehearsal flashes. Then compare the drum frames with the lamp frames.
lines: c8_lab.props.01
steve|They fell for a show once. So we put on another one. Live, this time.
props.finding: steve|The drums and lamps hit together on frames 120, 128 and 136; the fog just drifts. One cue drives the whole effect. Shaw’s reactor can play again, and this time we play it live.

lastpage.title: The last page
lastpage.goal: Find the sound Helen copied onto her last page.
lastpage.background: Helen’s last page is not shorthand. It is three pencil strokes copied from one of Frank’s hydrophone reels: two joined strokes climbing, a gap, then one long stroke lower than both.
lead: wen|Beside it she wrote: “From Frank’s tapes. I cannot read it, but I know a language when I hear one.”
wen|Three strokes. The second joins the first and climbs higher. Then a gap. Then a long stroke, lower than both.
steve|Dad wrote the pitch on every reel. A higher number means a higher note.
lastpage.prompt: Which reel did Helen draw, and what can Steve honestly write down?
lastpage.instruction: Helen’s page: two joined strokes climbing, a gap, then one long stroke lower than both. A higher number means a higher note. Reel 07: one long tone at 220 Hz. Reel 11: 220 Hz rising to 330 Hz, a gap, then a long 165 Hz. Reel 14: 220 Hz rising to 330 Hz, a gap, then a long 440 Hz.
hints: Read each reel as a shape. Does each tone go up or down?
Two reels start the same way. Only the last tone tells them apart.
Helen’s last stroke is lower than both before it. And she wrote that she cannot read it.
lines: c8_lab.lastpage.01
c8_lab.lastpage.02
lastpage.finding: steve|Mom’s last page is Dad’s Reel 11: two joined tones rising, 220 to 330, a half-second gap, then a long 165, lower than both. Her margin says it repeats after the low note. It’s a language, and nobody on Earth can read it.

recap: steve|Two countries faked two tests and broadcast them on open radio. Something out there was listening, and it came. Mom heard the proof in the bay.
steve|Shaw’s reactor still works, if one cue drives the drums and lamps. And Mom’s last page is a language from Dad’s tapes that nobody can read.

outro.new: steve|Mrs. Penhallow was standing by the reactor. Nobody had seen her come in.
steve|When I turned round, she was gone.

outro.text: Midnight tomorrow, Madam President. The ninth night. The engine, or the scan resumes.
outro.direction: from every screen and radio in the county

outro.new: saren|And Mr. Mercer. Come down to the beach at dawn. Alone.

lines: steve|You knew my mother nine years ago. What was she like in that room?
wen|Tired, like all of us. But she brought a tin of lemon cookies and shared them with both sides.
wen|Nobody refuses a cookie from the interpreter. It was very clever of her.
wen|I walked here from the hotel. An old woman with a dog said good morning to me in Mandarin.
steve|In Mandarin? Out here in Bellwether?
wen|Perfect Mandarin. Then she asked me if I needed any bait.
steve|How long have you two known each other?
wen|Nine years. We were enemies for one week and friends ever since.
wen|She still owes me a dinner. She lost a bet about the fog machine.
steve|Are those really washing-machine drums?
shaw|Six of them, from a laundromat in Reno. The owner thought I was starting a business.
shaw|In a way, I was.
shaw|Thirty years of explosions, and I can still hear a mouse cough in the next room.
steve|So can I. It makes the cinema very hard.
shaw|Sit in the back row. Nobody coughs in the back row.

second.goal: Find out whether Mom really sent that message.
second.background: Mom’s voicemail from the night of the boat is on the cassette in Steve’s cardigan pocket, and Dad’s recorder can play it. Rook took that cassette at the safe house and handed it back an hour later. Steve has played it at three in the morning for eighteen months. He knows every breath in it.

wrong.0: Listen to the breath before “kiddo”. It’s the same breath, from the same night.

lines.new: steve|Rook kept this tape for an hour at the safe house. Long enough to copy it.

second.finding: steve|Saren’s message is Mom’s voicemail, cut and stitched: the same breath before ‘kiddo’, and a gap where ‘The bay is singing’ used to be. He has no message from her. He has my tape.

refuse.title: The notebook
refuse.background: Mom’s notebook proves there is no engine. If Saren has it, the fleet learns that Earth has nothing to defend itself with. His only proof that Mom and Dad are coming home is a voice he cut out of a voicemail.
hints: There is nothing to solve here.
There is nothing to solve here.
Keep the notebook.

lines.text: That’s my voicemail. You cut my mother out of her own message. No. You don’t get to trade the whole town for my family.

refuse.finding: steve|I kept the notebook. Saren had a promise, my mother’s voice cut to fit it, and nothing else.

recap: steve|Saren offered me my parents for Mom’s notebook. His proof was my own voicemail, cut to say what he wanted.
steve|I said no. And for the first time I wondered how many times he’d done this before.

outro.text: How many families on Tirel got a message like that?

outro.new: steve|He was quiet for a long time.

c8_rig.objective: Build a show the ship will measure for itself, and plan the way in.

context: steve|Back at Sentinel Point, I told them the plan. It had a lot of holes. Shaw filled most of them with gaffer tape.

source.title: Signal sources
source.goal: Find the one feed that answers live.
source.background: The old tests repeated one recorded pulse, and anyone who compared them could tell. Steve’s show must answer every cue live. Wen has three feeds on three covered jacks: Birch, Ash and Elm.
lead: wen|Three feeds, three jacks. Shaw, give me a cue.
wen|One jack carries my lamp tester. It flashes on beat five, every time.
shaw|One carries my rehearsal film, looping on beat four. And one is my own hand on the button.
wen|Shaw cued beat four, then beat seven. Birch flashed on five both times. Ash flashed on four both times.
wen|Elm flashed on four, then on seven. It followed her.
source.prompt: Which feed is behind each jack, and which one answers Shaw live?

board.instruction: Match each jack to the feed behind it.
evidence: Wen’s lamp tester always flashes on beat 5.
Shaw’s rehearsal film loops on beat 4, whatever she does.
Shaw’s own hand follows whatever cue she gives.
Shaw cued beat 4, then beat 7. Birch flashed on 5 and 5, Ash on 4 and 4, and Elm on 4 and 7.

stages.prompt: Put one card on each jack.

board.wrong_text: Wen shakes her head. “Something in there is a recording pretending to listen.”

hints: One trial can’t tell a live feed from a loop. Look at what changed when Shaw changed her cue.
A tester and a film do the same thing every time. Only a hand can follow a new cue.
Which jack flashed on a different beat when Shaw changed hers?
lines: c8_rig.source.01
source.finding: steve|Birch is Wen’s fixed tester, stuck on beat 5. Ash is Shaw’s rehearsal loop, stuck on 4. Elm follows Shaw’s hand, live. Only Elm can answer a cue nobody has seen before.

path.title: Trust path
path.goal: Get the show into the ship’s own measurements, and get the sleepers out.
path.background: The fleet trusts only its own ship. A camera picture or numbers sent from shore prove nothing to them. And if the ship leaves, it takes three hundred sleepers with it.
lead: wen|I ran a paper trial. Three receipts. Only one of them would convince me, if I were them.
wen|The dock receipt says a camera saw the lamps. The mast receipt says the ship measured them. The shore receipt says the ship got our crew’s numbers.
wen|The fleet trusts nothing that its own ship did not measure.
stephen|My crew pass still opens the antenna passage. I checked. Twice. Cancelling it would put Saren’s mistake on the record.
steve|And the sleepers are in the Gallery. Mom and Dad are in row nine.
path.prompt: Which receipt will the fleet accept, and who does what?
path.instruction: The fleet trusts only what its own ship measured. Dock: a camera saw the lamps. Mast: the ship measured the lamps. Shore: the ship received numbers from our crew. Only a crew pass opens the antenna passage. The sleepers are in the Gallery.

rows.label: What does everyone else do?
options: Bring the sleepers out of the Gallery

hints: In each receipt, who did the measuring?
Only one receipt has the ship itself doing the measuring.
Give Stephen the job that needs a crew pass. Everyone else goes where the sleepers are.

rig.title: Props and radio
rig.goal: Pick the coupler Stephen will carry to the antenna.
rig.background: The coupler sits between Shaw’s console and the ship’s antenna. It must send Shaw’s cue out and keep the stage hum from coming back, or the ship will hear a theater instead of a show.
lead: stephen|Three couplers, identical plugs. I’d like the one that works.
wen|I tested all three twice. Once to see the cue go out, and once to hear what leaks back.
shaw|We need a signal going out and nothing coming back. Otherwise the ship hears my theater.
wen|Careful. A dead coupler also lets nothing back. It looks perfect until you check the cue.
rig.prompt: Which coupler sends the cue and keeps the hum out?

board.instruction: Wen tested each coupler twice. Match each one to what it does.
evidence: A good coupler sends Shaw’s cue out and lets no stage hum back.
Cue going out: A reads 8, B reads 0, C reads 8.
Hum coming back: A reads 5, B reads 0, C reads 0.
A dead coupler also lets nothing back, so check both readings.

stages.prompt: Put one card on each coupler.
pieces: Works: cue out, no hum back

board.wrong_text: Wen checks the meter again. One of those cards doesn’t fit the numbers.

hints: Read the two tests one at a time: the cue going out, then the hum coming back.
One coupler sends no cue at all. Another lets the hum back in.
A quiet return is only good if the cue also goes out. Which coupler does both?

c8_rig.rig.02
rig.finding: steve|Coupler A leaks the stage hum, B passes nothing, and C passes Shaw’s cue with a clean return. Stephen carries C to the antenna.

recap: steve|The plan: Shaw and Wen stage the Meridian test again, live, on Elm through coupler C. Stephen carries the rig into the ship’s antenna, so the ship measures the show for itself.
steve|The rest of us go to the Gallery and wake everyone, Mom and Dad included. Iris and Stephen voted for it, knowing what it costs them.

outro.new: steve|That night we went back under the bay, through the aquarium tunnel. Pell stayed behind with Biscuit. Ten minutes later he caught up with us, carrying her.

lines: steve|Did you water the balcony flowers before we left?
iris|This morning. The irises have two new buds. I counted them.
steve|Nora always forgot to water them. They nearly died twice.
iris|Then I’ll keep them alive until she’s home. That’s something I can do.

steve|What have you lost so far?

steve|I’m so sorry, Iris. Truly.
stephen|I’m writing a list on my hand. Steve, Mom, Dad, Biscuit.
steve|Biscuit made your list before the rest of the town?

shaw|I’ve used eleven rolls of gaffer tape today. That’s a personal record.
steve|Is that good news or bad news?
shaw|In my business, it means the show is nearly ready.
wen|I called my daughter last night. She asked what I’m building this time.
steve|What did you tell her?

steve|How’s your wrist, Madam President?
ward|Bandaged and famous. Half the country has seen it on television.
